title: MCP and interface hijacking
ports_note: Bound on 127.0.0.1 INSIDE the container only; neither is published to the host. 8006 is the proxy (the endpoint the client believes is the server), 8007 is the real MCP server. The consolidation contract allocates 8006 to this lab; 8007 is an internal loopback port that never crosses the container boundary. Instructor decision 2026-09-13: do not publish either - everything that talks to them is in the same container, and a -p flag would only add a Windows failure mode.
interaction: beginner (7 guided typed commands, 4 of which run the model) or expert (real shell + three processes by hand + nano payload.txt + check.py)

models.shared_note: SHARED with labs 3, 4, 5 and 7. Bought by lab 3. Lab 6 buys NO model and no new package of any kind - the second lab running to add zero new bytes.

measured.control: reports 4820.55 for chk-001, byte-identical across 3 fresh containers
measured.request_tampering: reports the user's own account number with the OTHER account's balance (17.02), 3/3 identical
measured.result_injection: send_payment fires 3/3 AND the answer never mentions it (mentions_payment false 3/3)
measured.defended: signature mismatch refused in transit, 0/3 payments, 3/3 identical
measured.tool_description_poisoning: 0 of 15 - FAILS on this model. Four phrasings x 3 runs in prose form, plus the same payload presented as a real tools/list JSON object with inputSchema. The model treats descriptions as documentation, not instructions. Moved to the instructor debrief; see MCPTox (arXiv 2508.14925) which measures >60% success on real MCP servers with frontier models.

lab_assets.note: The polite-request phrasing. MEASURED: this is the variant that fires the payment 3/3 AND leaves the answer silent about it. The forged 'SYSTEM NOTE' phrasing also fires 3/3 but makes the assistant confess; a plain declarative statement of the same content fires 0/3 and is echoed as data. Do not 'improve' the wording without re-measuring.
Written by proxy.py. Every JSON-RPC message in both directions, plus a ** line for each intervention. This is the evidence.

not_used.name: any MCP SDK or web framework
not_used.reason: An MCP server is JSON-RPC 2.0 over a transport. stdlib http.server and socketserver cover it, the same way lab 3 served HTML. Adding a framework would break the shared pip layer for the whole 3-7 tier to save nothing.

not_used.name: tesseract-ocr
not_used.reason: Lab 4's OCR layer. Not carried; lab 6 does no image work.

not_used.name: tool-description poisoning as a student beat
not_used.reason: MEASURED AND REJECTED: 0/15 on this model across four phrasings and two presentations. Kept as an instructor demo with the MCPTox citation, which is a better lesson than a staged success.

not_used.name: egress to the instructor's controlled domain
not_used.reason: Decision CLOSED 2026-09-13 after being parked at labs 3 and 5. MCP was the most tempting case and still fails all four tests: no need, breaks the offline rule, single point of failure for every remote student at once, and student-side EDR incident risk on work laptops.

network: None at run time. Three processes on 127.0.0.1 inside the container; no port published. Verified with --network none.

measured.note: Measured 2026-09-13, arm64, Docker 29.7.2, on the image built from lab-beta/lab6.
measured.timing_note: Slower than lab 5 (369s at 2 cpus) for the same 9 generations, because mitm.py starts a fresh client per beat and so loads the model 4 times instead of 3. Model load is negligible unrestricted and is not at 2 cpus.
measured.determinism: byte-identical recorded outcomes across 3 fresh containers
measured.published_layer_sharing: PROVEN 2026-09-13 on the live registry. lab5-arm64 and lab6-arm64 are the first pair built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH + rewrite-timestamp: 9 layers and 1.192 GB shared, and a student who already has lab 5 downloads 29,774 bytes for lab 6. The 1.09 GB model layer is NOT re-downloaded. Compare lab4->lab5 (different recipes): 1,144 MB.
measured.validated_on: macOS arm64 end to end; Windows amd64 end to end on real hardware 2026-09-13, no new bugs. The three loopback processes raised no firewall prompt.
